Question 'What did the customer say about their car?' returned an AI answer containing 'check engine light' with a Text citation chip ask-cite-T2 labelled 'Text'. Follow-up chips (3) contain NO '[' markers. Tapping ask-cite-T2 closed the sheet and navigated to /thread/6aa3673e65d794ba9962f1d6?jumpToMsg=6aa3673e65d794ba9962f1d8, thread rendered without crash and composer visible. (2) Rep (activation-tester) opening /contact/6aa413008f0d53e3f2261853 loaded the existing session (3 AI msgs); all 9 ask-follow-up chips have zero '[' characters, confirming client-side stripping of stored older follow-ups with [C1@..] markers. Only 1 new LLM question was used (within budget).

issues: thread-search-btn / thread-call-btn / thread-voice-memo-btn use a bare `data-testid` prop on TouchableOpacity which does not forward to DOM in RN Web (only `dataSet={{ testid: '...' }}` forwards, as used correctly by thread-ask-jessi-btn). Pills render visually but automation cannot locate them by data-testid. Recommend switching those three to the same dataSet pattern used by the Ask pill (thread/[id].tsx around lines 2236, 2252, 2259).

critical_code_review_comments: AskJessiSheet.tsx follow-up marker stripping now correct — verified against 9 legacy stored follow-ups and 3 freshly-generated ones. All render clean.
contact_ask.py access rule broadened correctly: manager on a shared-inbox conversation can now access /api/contact-ask/{contact_id} overview + ask endpoints. Verified with qa-manager on Lead 0033.

Thread [id].tsx line 2236/2252/2259: three header action pills use `data-testid=...` directly on RN TouchableOpacity, which is a no-op in RN Web. Use `dataSet={{ testid: '...' }}` or `testID` with expo-router web bridge. Aesthetic only — pills render, just not queryable by testid.

rca of the issue: Both fixes are effective. Fix #1 (contact_ask _contact access): the endpoint now grants access when the caller is a member/manager of an inbox that owns any conversation for the contact (or is assigned/collaborator). Fix #2 (follow-up stripping): AskJessiSheet renders follow-ups via a client-side sanitize that drops the `[TCVEK]n(@m:ss)?` tokens, so both new and stored-legacy follow-ups display clean text.
